4846.en: Let A'B'C' be the translation of ABC by the vector X_4X_3. Let M_{A} be the midpoint of the (possibly nonreal) points in which the circumcircle of ABC meets the line B'C', and define M_{B} and M_{C} cyclically. The triangle :g:`M_{A}M_{B}M_{C} << M_A M_B M_C >>` is perspective to ABC, and the perspector is X_4846.

4882.en: X_4882 = orthologic center of these triangles: excentral to Andromeda
re: X_4882 = orthologic center of these triangles: excentral to Andromeda
no: Consider any triangle ABC. Let A-excircle ω _A of ABC is tangent to BC at A'. Similarly define ω _B, ω _C, B', C'. Consider two tangent lines ℓ_{a}, ℓ_{a'} from A' to ω _B, ω _C which are different from BC. Similarly define ℓ_{b}, ℓ_{b'}, ℓ_{c}, ℓ_{c'}. Then ℓ_{a}, ℓ_{a'}, ℓ_{b}, ℓ_{b'}, ℓ_{c}, ℓ_{c'} form a hexagon which has an incircle. The center of the incircle of the hexagon is X_4882. (Angel Montesdeoca, October 2, 2018)
